answer: Interleaved arrival windows. Each identity's first N actions must arrive inside disjoint, randomly assigned time windows; agents that wander outside their window are throttled to one action per epoch. A shared vault of pending actions reveals overlapping timing signatures across identities; any identity matching another's arrival relic from a prior epoch is dropped. Attacker cost: must stagger sock puppets across many epochs, paying wall-clock delay and per-identity epoch fees.
